title: Lincoln Riley stresses 'belief' after USC's loss to Indiana crushes CFP hopes: 'Know how close we are' - CBS Sports
description: The Trojans coach's road struggles agains quality competition continue and this time, snuffed out a promising sea
body:
The Trojans coach's road struggles agains quality competition continue and this time, snuffed out a promising season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:41 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        So much for 18th-ranked USC barging into the College Football Playoff's backdoor this season.Saturday's 27-13 loss at No. 9 Indiana closes the book on CFP dreams for Lincoln Riley's Trojans, who needed to be perfect in the final weeks to emerge from the Big Ten as a potential national championship contender.Instead, it's a nine-win ceiling for a team equipped with a top-end roster whose lone ranked win came sandwiched between tough-to-stomach losses."I believe in what we're doing. I believe in myself," Riley said after USC's fourth-quarter struggle against the Hoosiers. "I believe in our leadership. I believe in our administration, and I believe everything happening here. Trust me, there's nobody that wants it as bad as all of us involved. We know how close we are as a group and we know how close were as a team. 
"We got a good view of that tonight.  We're going to keep battling. We will get there. And all of this will continue to make it more sweet when that time does happen."With job security concerns in the rearview since recovering from the wretched showing at Wisconsin in October, USC was one of the few teams outside of the top-12 rankings to still be in control of its destiny before failures in crunch time against the Hoosiers.The win over Ohio State earlier this month appeared to be Riley's breakthrough moment at USC, but this latest loss was further indicative of his tenure-long struggles in the marquee matchups. He's now 6-15 against nationally ranked opponents as coach of the Trojans, which includes one victory in nine tries on the road.
USC dropped four interceptions — including three in the end zone — while quarterback Jayden Maiava tossed three picks, one going to Indiana linebacker Isaiah Jones at the 5-yard line in a one-possession game. Maiava only had five total on the season coming into this one."We just had too many mistakes," Riley said. "We played hard, thought we played physical. I thought we were really resilient throughout the game. … We did a good job putting ourselves there, but we gotta go shut the door, and we understand that."Riley read a prepared statement after USC's win over Ohio State, but had nothing of the sort after losing to Indiana. It was simply more of the same dialogue uttered after other losses in other similar spotlight opportunities.
"We've come a long way as a program, but obviously, we have a little ways to go," Riley said. "And closing out games like that is what you've got to do to be the best. We're right there, close tonight, and this game came down to a couple of plays. But we've got to shut the door and get back to work. "We're going to get back on the plane to LA, correct what we needed to correct, and move on to the next one."That "next one" is the home finale against Maryland with considerably less at stake on Nov. 21 before heading to Pasadena to battle unbeaten UCLA in the finale. The Bruins can clinch a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game under first-year coach Bob Chesney with a win over Michigan before playing the Trojans.

title: Rory McIlroy wins record 8th Race to Dubai; Tyrrell Hatton takes DP World Tour title - CBS Sports
description: It came down to the wire, but McIlroy emerged as the top man in Europe once again, this time to conclude the 2026
body:
It came down to the wire, but McIlroy emerged as the top man in Europe once again, this time to conclude the 2026 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Rory McIlroy has done it again. The 37-year-old played just well enough Sunday at Jumeirah Golf Estates to claim a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai crown on the DP World Tour, pulling him alongside Colin Montgomerie for most all-time. The 2026 triumph marks McIlroy's fifth in a row, but this one was not without drama as McIlroy ultimately eked past Eugenio Chacarra, who entered the week in pole position, to claim the title."I don't really know what to say. ... Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," McIlroy said. "I remember Monty being obviously a stalwart of the European Tour, going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years. I remember playing with him for the first time at The London Club at The European Open in 2008. "So, to pull up alongside him and to win eight of these things, yeah, it means the world to me. I'm a very proud European. I'm a proud European player. I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour. Yeah, I'm very proud of myself right now."While McIlroy claimed the season-long race, Tyrrell Hatton was victorious at Sunday's season-ending 2026 DP World Tour Championship.
One week after his former LIV Golf teammate, Jon Rahm, won in Abu Dhabi, the Englishman followed suit in relatively stress-free fashion. Hatton finished the tournament at 15 under, good for a five-stroke victory over McIlroy, who finished in solo second. Chacarra slotted in a tie for third place with Oliver Lindell."This is really special. I was really nervous today," Hatton said. "I didn't say anything to anyone on my team or even to Emily. Yeah, I've had a bit of heartbreak around here, and I felt like it was going to be a difficult day. Just really proud of how I played on the back nine. Putter was amazing. Certainly saved me all week. It feels so good to win here."McIlroy entered the weekend projected to win the Race to Dubai only for Chacarra to reclaim the top spot heading into Sunday. In the final round, McIlroy was magnificent. The world No. 2 turned in 4-under 32 and bided his time to make one last move.
A string of six straight pars gave way to a beautiful wedge shot into the par-4 16th. With water lining the right side of the green, McIlroy struck his best approach of the afternoon to set himself up for what proved to be a season-defining birdie.
"This is probably a good thing, but I wasn't aware of how much it was sort of going back and forth until the 16th," McIlroy said. "When I was walking to the green, I saw that he was projected 1. Then when I made my birdie, and I'm walking off the green, I saw I was projected 1. I was a little nervous going to the last couple of holes. "I guess I did what I needed to do, and I shot a good score today. A lot of other things went my way today, as well. No one made a run. Eugenio played pretty good, but none of the chasing pack did anything. ... Thankfully, everything fell my way today."
McIlroy's final tally came in at 10 under, a number Chacarra nearly leveled on his front nine. The 26-year-old Spaniard was 4 under through his first eight holes and 9 under for the tournament with 10 holes to play. After making three bogeys in a four-hole stretch, Chacarra countered with birdies on Nos. 13-14, pulling him 0.10 points ahead of McIlroy in the Race to Dubai.Chacarra was unable to add another birdie coming in, and with McIlroy's birdie on No. 16 to push his total to 10 under and in solo second place, the fate of the two was out of their hands. Chacarra required another to pull even with McIlroy and effectively take points away from the Northern Irishman, but it never came to be for the former Oklahoma State Cowboy.
"It was a good fight. I just came out short," Chacarra said. "That's the beauty of golf, obviously, when you play with the best in the world. And he's played here 14, 15 times; you knew it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did."
For his season-long efforts, Chacarra leads the 10 players to earn PGA Tour cards for the 2027 season. By finishing atop this group, he will have access to the first two signature events and The Players Championship. Joining him is another LIV Golf alumnus, Patrick Reed, who held the lead in the Race to Dubai for most of the season before falling flat these last two weeks.Reed will return to the circuit he called home for many years alongside newcomers Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper, Daniel Hillier, Jacob Skov Olesen and Oliver Lindell, who fired a final round, bogey-free 65 to earn his card. Former European Ryder Cupers Andy Sullivan and Bernd Wiesberger locked up their PGA Tour cards as well with 32-year-old Englishman Joe Dean securing the final ticket.

title: Oregon gets an 'A' mark while Texas earns 'C-' on Week 8 report card - CBS Sports
description: A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 11 action
body:
A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 11 action
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:42 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        How serious is Alabama's offense problem? The No. 5 Crimson Tide have won three straight SEC games by double digits after a 21-6 victory at Vanderbilt on Saturday, but don't let the final scores obscure a deeper truth. While the defense is coming up clutch, the offense is trending in a bad direction. It won't matter next week against Wofford, and it might not matter the next week against rival Auburn. But if Alabama shows up in the postseason with this rushing attack, it probably won't last long. Alabama has averaged fewer than 3 yards per rush in each of its past four games. That marks a notable downtick after the Tide averaged 3.9 yards per rush or better over their first six games.Alabama escaped with a win over the Commodores, despite averaging just 4.5 yards per play. The only time Alabama averaged fewer yards per play was in a 26-10 loss at Tennessee. The version of Alabama's offense that totaled 200+ rushing yards against South Carolina and Georgia has gone MIA.This is an issue for the Crimson Tide, and it's why they aren't receiving a better grade for a 15-point SEC road win.
We are handing out grades evaluating every team that started or ended the day with national championship odds of +3000 or better. 2026 national championship odds listed below courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Teams listed in order of their AP Top 25 ranking.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 GeorgiaGrade: A  Result: 48-21 win vs. Missouri  Title odds: +210It was clear what direction this was headed from the first play, when Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception. Georgia proceeded to take a 31-0 lead in its second straight blowout of a ranked conference opponent. Coming out of Week 11, the Bulldogs are the preeminent force in college football and wholly deserving of their status as the national title favorite. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 UtahGrade: B+  Result: 40-39 win at Arizona  Title odds: +2500Utah survived three turnovers inside a hostile venue to escape with its unbeaten record intact. The defense wasn't perfect, either, but the Utes produced four big sacks and didn't let Arizona move the football when the game hung in the balance late. After traveling to Tucson early Saturday, this was just one the Utes had to get through. Thanks to another huge game from star quarterback Devon Dampier, they accomplished the mission.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 AlabamaGrade: C+  Result: 21-6 win at Vanderbilt  Title odds: +500Alabama entered with the SEC's No. 4 third-down defense and will only be going up after holding Vanderbilt to 3 of 19 on third- and fourth-down plays. This was another example of defensive coordinator Kane Wommack's unit carrying the day as the Crimson Tide racked up nine tackles for loss. With the offense too often looking rudderless, Bama needs its defense to continue delivering.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 UCLAGrade: B  Result: 22-14 win vs. Illinois  Title odds: +3000UCLA followed a familiar formula while improving to 10-0 against Illinois. The Bruins won the turnover battle, limited the opponent's run game and did just enough offensively in critical moments. On a night when star running back Wayne Knight rarely broke loose, quarterback Ty Dieffenbach gritted through injury and delivered some critical throws. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Notre DameGrade: A  Result: 41-7 win vs. Boston College  Title odds: +370Notre Dame led 31-0 at halftime before calling off the dogs to rest up for next week's SMU game. The yardage difference through two quarters was 287-46, and Boston College had just two first downs. Coming off an emotional win over No. 1 Miami, this was a mature showing from the Fighting Irish as they dominated in all facets. The Eagles averaged a measly 2.6 yards per play.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 TexasGrade: B  Result: 22-21 win at LSU  Title odds: +850Arch Manning threw the game-winning touchdown pass, but only after another game full of sacks, interceptions and missed throws. The Longhorns went more than 55 minutes between touchdowns and needed their defense to do some heavy lifting down the stretch. Ultimately, a night win inside Death Valley can't be graded too harshly. But let's not pretend this team has turned the proverbial corner.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 MiamiGrade: B  Result: 36-25 win vs. Duke  Title odds: +1000No Malachi Toney, no problem. After a jittery start, Miami's offense carried the day, as Darian Mensah kept his Heisman campaign on track with a 382-yard passing performance. Like most teams, the Hurricanes struggled to contain Duke star back Nate Sheppard, who amassed 224 yards as a runner and receiver. But it was encouraging to see the offense get in rhythm amid its second game without Toney.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 TennesseeGrade: BResult: 22-7 win at Texas A&MTitle odds: +3000Tennessee isn't going to win a beauty contest, but its defense is vicious. A Texas A&M offense that was already struggling stood no chance against coordinator Jim Knowles' swarming unit. The Aggies totaled just 179 yards and eight first downs as the Volunteers possessed the ball for more than 42 minutes. A lackluster passing game puts a ceiling on Tennessee's potential, but the defense can make it competitive against anyone.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 IndianaGrade: B+Result: 27-13 win vs. USCTitle odds: +900With quarterback Grant Wilson making his first start since 2024 and leading rusher Turbo Richard out, the Hoosiers hummed along with 7.3 yards per play. IU surrendered more yardage (409) than in any prior game under third-year coach Curt Cignetti. But the Hoosiers stepped up in critical situations by intercepting three passes and putting the clamps on USC in the red zone.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 21 LSUGrade: B-Result: 22-21 loss vs. TexasTitle odds: +125000 (+1400 entering day)Lane Kiffin's first season at LSU will go down as a major disappointment because the Tigers could not figure out how to win close games against quality opposition. LSU's offense remains too reliant on Sam Leavitt, and his interception problems returned with a vengeance against Texas. The Tigers were also heavily penalized (13 for 108 yards). And while they played good defense, they couldn't get a stop with the game — and their CFP hopes — on the line.

title: UFC 334 fight fallout: Next options for Ciryl Gane, Josh Hokit, Kayla Harrison and more - CBS Sports
description: Gane should keep a close eye on UFC 335 next month when Sergei Pavlovich takes on Alex Pereira
body:
Gane should keep a close eye on UFC 335 next month when Sergei Pavlovich takes on Alex Pereira

    9:30 am ET

        Ciryl Gane and Kayla Harrison leave Madison Square Garden on Saturday with UFC titles still in their possession. The fallout from the event raises interesting questions about the heavyweight and women's bantamweight divisions, especially with UFC 335 on the horizon.The heavyweight division is finally finding its footing after years of uncertainty. Gane is the first undisputed UFC heavyweight champion to complete a successful title defense since Jon Jones beat Stipe Miocic two years ago. Alex Pereira and Sergei Pavlovich are set to meet next month, while Alexander Volkov continues holding firm near the top of the rankings. Opportunities are finally opening up in multiple directions for what was once MMA's premier division.Harrison and Amanda Nunes' futures are less clear. The women's bantamweight champion hinted at retirement, but Saturday's victory over the greatest women's fighter in MMA history might be enough to convince her to stick around. Nunes, meanwhile, must decide whether another fight is worth pursuing after coming up short in her comeback.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!With UFC 334 in the rearview mirror, let's take a look at the fights to make Saturday's biggest winners and losers.
HeavyweightCiryl Gane vs. Sergei Pavlovich or Alex Pereira: It's no accident that Pavlovich and Pereira are fighting one month after the heavyweight title fight. This is very likely a title eliminator. I think Pavlovich is a nightmare matchup for Pereira. If "Poatan" beats him, he'll likely have shown the improvements necessary to inspire hope that he can beat Gane in the rematch. If Pavlovich wins, we're headed towards a very compelling clash between two natural heavyweights with speed and power.Josh Hokit vs. Alexander Volkov: Look, Volkov should be fighting for the heavyweight title next. You won't hear any arguments from me. However, it's abundantly clear that UFC matchmakers aren't going in that direction. Volkov knows that, and it's why he's doing everything he can outside of the Octagon to drum up interest. It started when Volkov questioned UFC CEO and president Dana White at the UFC 333 press conference. He also produced a series of twin-themed memes involving him and UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski. Ahead of UFC 334, Volkov walked around Times Square, running a tongue-in-cheek charity drive for "special needs" fighter Hokit. It isn't particularly tasteful, but driving interest towards that fight is best for both men.Women's bantamweightKayla Harrison vs. Valentina Shevchenko: There are legitimate contenders waiting for Harrison. I just don't know if Harrison, who is flirting with retirement, will be drawn to them. So we'll talk about them a little later and shift the attention towards someone who could coerce another fight out of the women's bantamweight champion. Beating Nunes was the cherry on top of a remarkable combat sports career. She took out the greatest of all time. The only thing that could come close to that is beating Shevchenko, Nunes' neighbor on the women's MMA Mount Rushmore. Shevchenko will be at a major size and strength disadvantage, but she has the speed, technique and IQ to fight the way Nunes should have on Saturday. 
Amanda Nunes vs. Joselyne Edwards or Ailin Perez: Nunes should seriously contemplate retiring again. She tried to do something great and fell short. It did nothing to tarnish her reputation, but there's nothing more for the women's MMA G.O.A.T. to prove. Now, she has options if she insists on fighting again. Edwards is on an impressive run, beating Norma Dumont after scoring four straight finishes. The promotion valued her enough to make her the official back-up for Saturday's co-main event. That said, another option will draw more eyeballs. Perez has fought and twerked her way into the MMA consciousness. She's on a seven-fight win streak -- including one over Edwards -- beat Dumont in her last fight and is ranked No. 3 in the division. If Nunes retires, either woman is worthy of a title shot or a title eliminator.

title: Lane Kiffin created LSU's championship expectations. Now, he's struggling to live up to them - CBS Sports
description: Backed by a $40+ million roster, the Tigers sit at 6-4 with zero wins over ranked opponents after a gut-wrenching
body:
Backed by a $40+ million roster, the Tigers sit at 6-4 with zero wins over ranked opponents after a gut-wrenching collapse against Texas killed their CFP hopes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:01 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        BATON ROUGE, La. – Raleek Brown went in motion. Davohn Keys reacted late on the coverage. Arch Manning threw an easy touchdown. Texas wins 22-21. LSU's College Football Playoff hopes evaporated. And with them went any remaining benefit of the doubt for Lane Kiffin's debut season. "(Davohn) has him, so you know …" Kiffin said with an exasperated shoulder shrug. "A lot of plays before that." LSU entered the 2026 season as a swaggering, give-no-fu----, headline-generating machine. Kiffin swirled at the center of it. He trolled. He did hot yoga in opposing SEC cities. He wagged his finger in the face of the SEC as LSU went to war with the league over adding players who signed professional contracts for a fifth collegiate season. 
He didn't arrive in Baton Rouge promising a long-term rebuild. He arrived selling an immediate championship vision. "Imagine if we had pro players," Kiffin said confidently in his halftime interview during a Week 1 blowout win over Clemson. They sure could use them nine games later. The Tigers have gone just 3-4 since in games against Power Four competition, losing to the only four currently ranked teams (Ole Miss, Kentucky, Alabama, Texas) on their schedule. 
For most coaches, a 6-4 record, especially when they returned just eight starters, would be considered a solid building block late in their debut season. Not for Kiffin. There are no legitimate excuses to be made for one of the sport's most expensive rosters (maybe the most expensive) and one of the sport's highest-paid head coaches.  Kiffin, in his own way, owned that in the aftermath of an 11-point, second-half collapse against Texas. 
"I get it," Kiffin said. "Underperformance. It doesn't matter if the games have been close or if they go down to the last six seconds. I was brought here to win, and we need to win more than that."Kiffin, in his own way, also offered explanations for LSU's struggles. There were the last-play busts that cost the Tigers against Kentucky and Texas. Make those stops and LSU's record looks quite different. There are the special teams miscues – a missed 38-yard field goal just ahead of halftime could have made the difference for the Tigers – that have plagued the team all year. There is the barrage of turnovers that have come from Leavitt's frenetic play style. Kiffin pointed to Sarkisian's Texas roster as an explanation for LSU's shortcomings. 
Sarkisian, in Year 6 in Austin, didn't have a roster that looked like Texas' on Saturday night when he went 5-7 in his Longhorns debut. It took time to build that sort of depth for Texas to withstand the pressure and difficulty of an SEC slate. "You build things, and they take a little bit of time," Kiffin said. "Watch warmups. Those guys have done a great job building a team with size, with backups, with special teams players. "It didn't look like that his first year." Kiffin's comparison to Sarkisian is a fair argument. No Year 1 roster will be ideal for a coach's needs and preferences. 
But there is an obvious flaw in Kiffin's rationale: money. When Sarkisian inherited Texas' roster in 2021, the Longhorns weren't exactly a team on the scrap heap. Tom Herman went 7-3 the year prior. But Sarkisian had to build the roster his way. It was the early stages of the transfer portal and before name, image and likeness payments. Roster construction took more time. Kiffin shouldn't get that same patience. LSU more than doubled its roster investment this offseason, going from approximately $18-20 million in 2025 to well over $40 million in 2026, per sources. The Tigers went all-in to land Kiffin and gave him far more resources to work with than Brian Kelly had just one year prior. Sarkisian needed time to build Texas into his vision. Kiffin had the resources to build LSU into his vision immediately. That's the difference.
LSU will get better. Kiffin's track record of success – even if he is just 15-28 in his career against AP Top 25 opponents – indicates he'll eventually build LSU back up into a contender. Until then, however, Kiffin will be a piñata that fans and the media take a swing at over and over again. Realistically, that's an expectation trap of Kiffin's own creation. He could have taken the LSU job in a more restrained fashion. Less trolling. Less behind-the-scenes sniping of Ole Miss players. Fewer shots at his old employers in Oxford. More restraint in the portal and with trying to create an edge in the court system. But he can't help but shrug at the podium when asked about miscues. He can't help but follow up ownership of a loss with reasons for his roster's shortcomings. 
"Yes, we need to win games," Kiffin said. "But I also don't overreact. If we covered a guy on that last play or if that fumble comes out a second earlier or whatever, we're in here and none of these questions are happening, and you're like, 'What a great job! What an awesome way to finish.'"Lane, as my CBS Sports colleague John Talty would put it, just can't help being Lane.

UCLA puts its undefeated record to the test against blue blood Michigan, while LSU tries to knock off a playoff contenders in Knoxville. Georgia and Notre Dame will try to avoid let down spots as they play a pair of teams that lost big in Week 11. With that in mind, lines are out for some of the top matchups of Week 12 and there's value to be found. Tennessee has played with fire each of the past several weeks, and LSU's defense is perhaps the best on Tennessee's schedule.

body:
Indiana needs to bench Josh Hoover permanently, while Lane Kiffin's high-priced debut at LSU has already turned into an undeniable flop
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Grant Wilson is 25 years old, a seventh-year senior and Indiana's best option at quarterback. It's not a development anyone could have expected at the beginning of the season. Indiana added TCU quarterback transfer Josh Hoover, one of the most expensive portal QBs available. Hoover was a prolific quarterback under Sonny Dykes at TCU, though he struggled with turnovers and looked like a good bet to be the next QB to flourish in Curt Cignetti's system. It hasn't gone according to plan this season. Hoover has struggled with injuries and has never fully clicked in Bloomington. Cignetti pulled him in favor of Wilson in a comeback win over Minnesota. The Indiana coach decided after that game he was going with Wilson against USC regardless of Hoover's health.And while Cignetti was non-committal after Saturday's win over the Trojans that Wilson was the guy moving forward, he should be. Led by defensive coordinator Bryant Haines, the Hoosiers again have one of the nation's best defenses. That was evident against USC.
What it needs is a competent quarterback who doesn't crumble under pressure and can make big plays. That's Wilson, who finished with 305 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He certainly wasn't perfect – he should have thrown a second interception in the second half – but Indiana needs more big-play ability from the quarterback position given injuries and its run game struggles. And when Wilson hit Nick Marsh for a 65-yard gain, it made all the sense in the world why Cignetti gave him the start.It's not easy to bench a veteran player like Hoover, especially knowing the money invested in him to be the starter. But it had been obvious for weeks there was something off about this Indiana team. All those concerns weren't magically washed away with a single win, but what we saw against the Trojans more closely matched what we expected out of a Cignetti-led team. In what feels like the most wide-open college football season in recent memory, Indiana's best chance to repeat as champion is sticking with the guy who signed with Fordham out of high school and before Saturday had last started a game for Old Dominion back in 2024. 
Lane Kiffin fails in first season at helmThe hopes Lane Kiffin had for his debut LSU season officially went up in smoke on a brilliant call from his old colleague Steve Sarkisian. As Raleek Brown raced to the end zone on a game-winning touchdown pass from Arch Manning, Kiffin watched in agony as another golden opportunity for a top-10 win slipped through his fingers. The man who infamously left a College Football Playoff-bound Ole Miss team because he didn't believe the program could win a national championship will not make the playoff this season. The 6-4 Tigers are officially out after a 22-21 loss to the Longhorns.Was it worth it?There's no debate that Kiffin and LSU failed to meet expectations this season. LSU made Lane one of the nation's highest-paid coaches in America, a seven-year, $91 million contract that pays him $13 million annually, to at least make the playoff. Losing four SEC games in Year 1 – the first LSU coach to do so since Curley Hallman – is not acceptable in Baton Rouge. Especially when you have what could be the nation's most expensive roster in the $50-million range, according to sources. 
Kiffin couldn't get his preferred transfer quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss, and chose poorly on the very expensive one, Sam Leavitt, whom he did get. Leavitt is entertaining to watch if you enjoy chaotic backyard-style football, but his three interceptions and poor decision-making against Texas highlighted his liabilities. Paying Leavitt more than what multiple Power Four head coaches make hasn't been a great investment for the Tigers.It's not hard to wonder what could have been had Lane stayed in Oxford. He would still have Chambliss as his quarterback, Pete Golding as his defensive coordinator and a roster built to win in 2026. Kiffin says he hasn't thought twice about his decision to leave – and there are plenty of folks in Oxford who are happy that he left – but Ole Miss and Lane may both be worse off without each other in 2026. The Rebels are also currently projected to miss the College Football Playoff. The timing was awful, but one could understand why Lane wanted to be at LSU. Two men Lane knew well, Nick Saban and Ed Orgeron, had both won national championships there. LSU had a fertile recruiting base, a large and rabid group of fans and significant institutional support from the Governor of Louisiana on down. It was the biggest attraction in the Bayou State. 
The question, though, was how Lane Kiffin would handle the pressure that came with being LSU's head coach. He badly wanted another shot at a blueblood program, questioning whether he'd ever get another shot after his USC firing in 2013. But the seasons in which Lane has faced the most pressure and expectations, he's faltered.In 2012, when USC was the preseason No. 1 team, the Trojans finished 7-5 and unranked. Players and coaches on that team told me for my book, "Lane Being Lane: The Story of Lane Kiffin, College Football's Agent of Chaos," that the expectations impacted how Kiffin coached.The year Lane faced the most expectations at Ole Miss, in 2024, he again faltered with inexplicable losses to Kentucky and Florida that doomed what should have been a playoff season. His best year came the following season in what looked like it might be a transition season before Chambliss took over for an injured Austin Simmons and the Rebels caught fire. It wasn't enough to keep Lane at Ole Miss but he seemed to coach his best when free of heavy outside pressure.
Unfortunately for Lane, the pressure in Baton Rouge will only ratchet up from here. A disappointing debut puts more pressure to at least make the expanded 24-team playoff in 2027. But even that ultimately won't be enough to be a genuine success at LSU. Brian Kelly made the SEC Championship Game his first season, went 34-14 and was still run out in less than four seasons. Kiffin was brought in to win national championships. Can he deliver? The narrative around his big-game struggles has only been bolstered by his early results at LSU. For all the hype Kiffin generates and all the big celebrities like Kevin Costner he can convince to come to big games, he still can't win them. With the loss to the Longhorns, Kiffin is now 6-19 against top-10 teams and 15-28 all-time against top-25 opponents. Lane Kiffin was willing to walk away from his first playoff team for the hope of something more at LSU. If that was the right decision can't be judged off a single season.  But whether he can make enough progress this offseason to meet even higher expectations next season is the question that could define his LSU tenure. 
Welcome back to the hot seat, Luke FickellLuke Fickell looked like the lone survivor. Of the four coaches CBS Sports identified on the hottest seats entering the season, Fickell was the only one making positive progress. The other three – Baylor's Dave Aranda, Florida State's Mike Norvell and Maryland's Mike Locksley – were all fired. With a 24-7 win over USC in late October, Fickell appeared to be off the hot seat and in good shape to return as Wisconsin's coach in 2027.That may have all changed with a devastating road loss to Maryland on Saturday. Led by interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim and backup quarterback Cardell Williams, the Terrapins stunned the Badgers and put Fickell right back on the hot seat. Industry sources have told CBS Sports throughout the season that Wisconsin wasn't eager to fire Fickell and pay a $20 million buyout to jump into the coaching carousel. Fickell won enough in the first two-thirds of the season to justify that stance. But the calls for change, especially from fans and boosters, are going to get louder in the aftermath of the Maryland loss. The Badgers now sit at 6-4 with two winnable games against Purdue and Minnesota remaining. Does Fickell now need to win out to feel secure? 
Jake Dickert, Wake Forest handled it perfectlyGive credit to Wake Forest athletic director John Currie and football coach Jake Dickert for taking a major distraction off the table in agreeing to a contract extension ahead of this weekend.Even in a quieter coaching carousel, Dickert was the hottest candidate in the country. His success at Wake Forest (and previous success at Oregon State) ensured his name would be mentioned for every job that opens this cycle. Understandably, that can be a big distraction for the coach, the team and everyone else associated with the program. Which is why I loved Dickert and Wake Forest striking a deal during the season. It's similar to a move Indiana and Curt Cignetti made a year ago when his name started coming up for openings like Penn State. We all know how that worked out for Indiana.
So far, so good for Wake Forest, too. The Demon Deacons crushed SMU, 49-7, in a win that should put Wake Forest into the playoff. Wake Forest is now 9-1 and in good position to make the field if it can win out against Georgia Tech and Duke. It's an incredible success story for the North Carolina program that hasn't gotten as much national attention as its rivals in the Research Triangle. Dickert and Wake Forest are on the precipice of accomplishing something never before done at Wake Forest. Good on all parties for recognizing that's more important than letting the possibility of Dickert leaving for another job hang over the remainder of the season. It was fun while it lasted, KentuckyDon't cry because it's over, Kentucky fans; smile because it happened at all. Kentucky's 21-14 home loss to Florida ends what was one of my favorite storylines of the season. Under first-year coach Will Stein, Kentucky rose all the way up to No. 6 in the country after wins over LSU, South Carolina and Oklahoma. The back-to-back walk-off wins off two-point conversions were electrifying. The path to the College Football Playoff was tangible. 
Unfortunately, those hopes have been dashed. Consecutive losses to Tennessee and Florida have badly damaged the Wildcats' playoff hopes. With its loss to Florida, Kentucky's playoff odds dropped to 2.5%, according to CBS Sports' forecasting model. Even if Kentucky wins out against Missouri and Louisville, it may finish with only one top-25 win after South Carolina lost to Arkansas and Missouri's blowout loss to Georgia. That won't be enough to get it ahead of other potential three-loss SEC teams.

title: Arch Manning on Texas eliminating LSU from CFP race: 'We talked about the chance to end someone else's dream' - CBS Sports
description: The Longhorns' star quarterback led a comeback for the ages in the final quarter in Baton Rouge
body:
The Longhorns' star quarterback led a comeback for the ages in the final quarter in Baton Rouge
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:32 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With a moment for the ages inside Tiger Stadium, Texas quarterback Arch Manning delivered late-game heroics that will never be forgotten in Longhorns football lore.Manning's 4-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown on a dart to the boundary with three seconds left lifted sixth-ranked Texas to a 22-21 win over No. 21 LSU, nullifying Lane Kiffin and the Tigers' shot at reaching the College Football Playoff this season.After trailing 21-10 midway through the third quarter, the Longhorns scored 12 unanswered points the rest of the way to push closer to a first-round home game or potential top-four seed in the CFP."We talked about having the chance to end someone else's dream, and I like to focus on us, but it kind of feels good at times," Manning said after his fifth win this season over an opponent currently ranked in the CFP's top 25.
Manning executed to near-perfection in the final moments, overcoming a three-interception outing with a couple of critical third-down conversions after Texas started its game-winning possession on its own 42-yard line trailing by five points with 2:19 left."It means the world," Manning said. "I was pointing out to some of my teammates where I sat at these games growing up. So, just coming back home, getting it done in the last few seconds, it's a memory I'll have for the rest of my life."It marked a homecoming of sorts for Manning in Louisiana, who played prep football at Isidore Newman in New Orleans as the nation's No. 1 overall recruit in the 2023 cycle. TV cameras showed Manning trot over to his father, Cooper, after the game, where the first row of seats begins just beyond the end zone, and share a quick embrace.
"It hadn't been great all night; I figured it was time to get it done," Manning said. "I grew up around a lot of LSU fans. So, it's going to feel good to come back for Mardi Gras, or come back whenever I come home (to New Orleans), and not have them talk a bunch of crap."Kiffin laments disappointing first seasonAt 6-4 overall and likely outside of CFP's third rankings on Tuesday night after another loss, LSU's path to an at-large appearance in the 12-team bracket is squashed.Despite spending more money than any program nationally on transfer portal acquisitions with the nation's top-rated class, the Tigers have largely failed to deliver during the season's most important spots. LSU doesn't have a ranked win and now needs to win out just to get one of the SEC's upper-tier bowl destinations.
Not that any of the postseason discussion matters without a CFP berth."I get it," Kiffin said after the game. "Underperformance doesn't matter if the game's been close or they go down to the last, whatever, six seconds. We were brought here to win, and we need to win more than that. Now, also, everything isn't built for the first year when you come in somewhere, and I would tell you that if we were undefeated right now. You build things, and they take a little bit of time."Kiffin said he wasn't "overreacting" to LSU's fourth loss and understands his program was on the brink this fall despite execution failures."I'm concerned that we lost. I'm not concerned about the future," Kiffin said. "I said it weeks before when we were winning, that we'll have better rosters. And that's no poor reflection upon these players. We just will. We will have been here. We'll have built depth. We won't have senior days with two scholarship players."
